title: Cracking, Reforming and Gasoline Quality
notes: **Cracking:** breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones by heat or catalyst. Thermal cracking: high temperature, no catalyst. Catalytic cracking: lower temperature, silica-alumina catalyst gives branched alkanes.
**Reforming:** rearranging straight-chain alkanes into branched-chain and aromatic hydrocarbons using $Pt/Al_2O_3$ catalyst at high temperature. Increases octane number.
**Octane number:** measure of gasoline quality. Iso-octane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) = 100; n-heptane = 0. Higher octane means resistance to knocking.
**Antiknocking:** knocking occurs when fuel auto-ignites before the spark. High compression engines need high-octane fuel.
**Cetane number:** measure of diesel quality. Cetane ($C_{16}H_{34}$) = 100. Higher cetane means shorter ignition delay and smoother combustion.
**Gasoline additives:** tetraethyl lead (PbEt$_4$) boosts octane but is phased out due to lead pollution. Replaced by MTBE, ethanol, and aromatics.
